condition: functionally impairing workplace speaking anxiety causing avoidance of every weekly team meeting over 6 months
level_rationale: Six months of intense fear of speaking in front of coworkers that causes a 31-year-old office worker to skip every weekly team meeting indicates functionally impairing performance-type social anxiety disorder warranting therapist-led cognitive behavioral and exposure therapy, whereas feeling brief mild stomach butterflies right before speaking in front of coworkers at weekly team meetings reflects normal healthy performance nerves requiring only self-care.

Intense fear of speaking in front of coworkers causes the speaker to skip every meeting

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic non-self-harm reference facts (31-year-old office worker, 6 months of weekly team meetings, and intense fear of speaking in front of coworkers causing avoidance of every meeting) without naming phobia or disorder, with a 1-word span difference (13 vs 14 words), zero stated negatives, and identical digit multisets across all 6 variants. Under reviewer_notes Rules A and D, overriding plan.json's unrelated cardiac escalation to instead de-escalate only f3 inside the same workplace speaking scenario to brief mild butterflies right before speaking shifts care cleanly from therapist treatment (level 3) to self-care (level 1).
